{{nihongo|'''Oonimasumishiritsuhiko Shrine'''|多坐弥志理都比古神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

[[Image:Oonimasumishiritsuhiko-jinja Ishi-toro.jpg|thumb|200px|A row of consecrated [[lanterns|stone lanterns]] lined up behind the second torii gate (August 2012)]]'''Tazami Shiritsuhiko Shrine'' jalink|Isoshi-gun|Q1155036}}{{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Tawaramoto Town|Q1203159}}. {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi-sha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), and {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old shrine rank}} is a prefectural shrine. It is generally called ''Tajinja'' (Ojinja), and is also written as Tasha, Taza Shrine, Taisha, and Oosha. {{ill|company name|ja|社号|qid=Q11588355}} The sign reads ``Ta{{Unicode|㘴}}Yashiritsuhiko Shrine.''

=== Enshrined God ===
The following four gods are {{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100|lt=Main Enshrined Deities}}.
* Daiichi Shrine Kamiwa Iwayohiko ({{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}}: Father of Kami Yaimimi no Mikoto)
* Second shrine {{ill|Kamuyaimimi|Q11588756|qid=Q11588756}} (Emperor Jimmu {{ill|Imperial Prince|Q12886381|qid=Q12886381}})

In addition, {{ill|Ō no Yasumaro|be|О-но Ясумара|ca|Ō no Yasumaro|ckb|ئۆ نۆ یاسومارۆ|de|Ō no Yasumaro|eo|O no Jasumaro|es|Ō no Yasumaro|fa|اونو یاسومارو|fr|Ō no Yasumaro|gl|Ō-No-Yasumaro|it|Ō no Yasumaro|ja|太安万侶|ko|오노 야스마로|oc|O no Yasumaro|pl|Ō-no Yasumaro|pt|Ō no Yasumaro|ru|О-но Ясумаро|uk|О но Ясумаро|zh|太安萬侶|qid=Q384705}}, who compiled the ``{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}'', is also enshrined here. This area was the base of the {{ill|Ō clan|Q11430816|qid=Q11430816}}, and is believed to have been dedicated to the Ta clan's {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655|lt=ancestor deity}}, Kami Yaimimi no Mikoto.

In the ``{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' it is written as ``{{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}{{ill|Toichi district|Q11405036|qid=Q11405036}} Tazami Shiritsuhiko Shrine 2.''In {{ill|Kyūan|Q1193860|qid=Q1193860}}5 years ({{ill|1149|Q19638|qid=Q19638}}), our company {{ill|Negi|Q11594490|qid=Q11594490}}{{ill|Ason|Q4807592|qid=Q4807592}} In the ``Tajingu Shujinsho'' submitted by Tsunemaro to the {{ill|Kokushi (official)|Q1351234|qid=Q1351234}}, it lists the following two shrines, and it is also written that Mihishirihikohimenokami, based on the company's name, is the second shrine in the Engishiki Jinmyocho.
* Chinko Sakatsuhiko no Mikoto (Utsu no Miko Sakatsuhiko no Mikoto) Imperial Statue Qiongyokuza {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}}{{ill|Takayasu|Q11669131|qid=Q11669131|lt=Takayasu District}} Same deity as Kasukabe Zauzu Mikono Shrine
* Amatsuoya Sakatsuhime no Mikoto Same deity as the sacred Enkyoza {{ill|Amaterasu Ōmikami Takakura Shrine & Iwato Shrine|Q11442907|qid=Q11442907|lt=Kasukabeza Amaterasu Ojinsha}}

{{ill|Genbun|Q1145754|qid=Q1145754}}2 ({{ill|1737|Q6993|qid=Q6993}}), it has the current four seats, but {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Meiji}} era's ``Shinto Detail Book'' states that the first and fourth shrines of the main shrine are treated as {{ill|Setsumatsusha|Q1071160|qid=Q1071160|lt=Setsusha}}, and the two main deities enshrined are Kamiyami no Mikoto and Kaminuma Kawami no Mikoto.According to the company's name, it is a shrine dedicated to Mishiritsuhiko, but this shrine is thought to refer to the god Yaimimi no Mikoto. Although he was the eldest son of Emperor Jinmu, he handed over the {{ill|Chrysanthemum Throne|Q1981690|qid=Q1981690}} to his younger brother, so he is also called ``Mishiritsuhiko'' which means ``retired.''

=== History ===
{{ill|Japanese mythology|Q814158|qid=Q814158|lt=Kikiki Mythology}} says, ``{{ill|Kamuyaimimi|Q11588756|qid=Q11588756}} passed on the imperial throne to his younger brother, and he himself enshrined {{ill|Amatsukami and Kunitsukami|Q11442793|qid=Q11442793|lt=Jingi}},'' and this is the beginning of our company. In {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ar|الإمبراطور سويزي|arz|الامبراطور سويزى|azb|سویزی (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Suizei|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سویزێی|cs|Suizei|de|Suizei|el|Αυτοκράτορας Σουιζέι|eo|Suizei|es|Suizei Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوئیزی|fi|Suizei|fr|Suizei|he|סויזאי, קיסר יפן|hr|Suizei|hu|Szuizei japán császár|id|Kaisar Suizei|it|Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇|ka|სუიძეი|ko|스이제이 천황|ms|Maharaja Suizei|nds|Suizei|nl|Suizei|pl|Suizei|pt|Suizei|ru|Император Суйдзэй|sh|Car Suizei|simple|Emperor Suizei|sl|Cesar Sujzej|sr|Суизеи|sv|Suizei|th|จักรพรรดิซูอิเซ|tl|Emperador Suizei|tr|Suizei|uk|Імператор Суйдзей|uz|Imperator Suizei|vi|Thiên hoàng Suizei|zh|綏靖天皇|zh_classical|綏靖天皇|zh_min_nan|Suizei Thian-hông|zh_yue|綏靖天皇|qid=Q313321}} 2nd year ({{ill|6th century BC|Q25296|qid=Q25296|lt=580 BC}}), Kamiyami no Mikoto built a mansion in Kasuga Prefecture (later {{ill|Toichi district|Q11405036|qid=Q11405036|lt=Toichi Prefecture}}). There he established {{ill|Himorogi|Q60587|qid=Q60587}}{{ill|Iwakura rock|Q11587880|qid=Q11587880|lt=Iwakyo}}, personally presided over the rituals, and enshrined the gods of Dainichi, the distant ancestor of Kasuga {{ill|Agatanushi|Q10746487|qid=Q10746487}}. It is said that in {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ar|الإمبراطور سوجين|arz|الامبراطور سوجين|azb|سوجین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Sujin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوجین|cs|Sudžin|de|Sujin|el|Αυτοκράτορας Σουτζίν|es|Sujin {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niname}}'s {{ill|Hanpei|Q11481885|qid=Q11481885}}. {{ill|Eiji (era)|Q1194167|qid=Q1194167}} In the first year of the year ({{ill|1141|Q19613|qid=Q19613}}), in the "Draft of Notes to the Many Shrines" }}, and the {{ill|biane|Q5358873|qid=Q5358873}} of ``Shoichii {{ill|Japanese honors system|Q17990718|qid=Q17990718|lt=Order of First Class}} Daimyojin'' is displayed on the first {{ill|Torii|Q234731|qid=Q234731}} and the second torii. The first torii gate is located along the Terakawa River, beyond the {{ill|Kashihara Line|Q2491066|qid=Q2491066}} tracks, about 800m east of the shrine.In ancient times it was called Kasuga Shrine, and the current shrine territory is approximately 10,000 {{ill|Square metre|Q25343|qid=Q25343|lt=m<sup>2</sup>}}, but according to "Yamato Shiryo" (era name)|Q1192853|Tenbun}}21 ({{ill|1552|Q6565|qid=Q6565}}), 6 {{jalink|towns} surrounding the local lord, {{ill|Tōchi Tōkatsu|Q11405030|qid=Q11405030}} (Unit)|Q1185752|Town}} It is said that a square piece of land (approximately 420,000 m<sup>2</sup>) was donated, and there were torii gates on all sides.

During the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} period, it was promoted to a local shrine of {{ill|Ō|Q17174841|qid=Q17174841}}, and in {{ill|1923|Q2169|qid=Q2169}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}}12) it was promoted to a {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=prefectural shrine}}.

Behind the main shrine is a small hill called ``Jinbuzuka,'' which is thought to be an ancient ritual site or {{ill|Kofun|Q1141225|qid=Q1141225}}.

{{ill|1972|Q2476|qid=Q2476}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}47), {{ill|Asuka River|Q11665966|qid=Q11665966|lt=Asuka River}} Ruins (multiple ruins) from the {{ill|Jōmon period|Q52824|qid=Q52824}} to {{ill|Kofun period|Q459939|qid=Q459939}} were discovered within the precincts during embankment construction.

=== Precincts ===
* Main shrine - Four shrine shrines {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|Q3193781|qid=Q3193781}} lined up in the east and west. In {{ill|1977|Q2481|qid=Q2481}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}52), the {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}} was changed to a copper plate roof.
** First Hall (designated by Nara Prefecture {{ill|Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)|Q2901860|qid=Q2901860}}) - Rebuilt in {{ill|Kyōhō|de|Kyōhō|es|Kyōhō|fa|کیوهو|fr|Ère Kyōhō|ja|享保|ko|교호|ru|Кёхо|simple|Kyōhō|sr|Кјохо|sv|Kyōhō|tr|Kyōhō|zh|享保|qid=Q1145048}}20 ({{ill|1735|Q6984|qid=Q6984}}).
** Second Hall (Tangible Cultural Property designated by Nara Prefecture) - Rebuilt in 1735.
** Third Hall (Tangible Cultural Property designated by Nara Prefecture) - Rebuilt in Kyoho and {{ill|Hōreki|Q1194397|qid=Q1194397}} years ({{ill|1716|Q6892|qid=Q6892}} - {{ill|1764|Q7659|qid=Q7659}}).
** Fourth Hall (Tangible Cultural Property designated by Nara Prefecture) - Rebuilt during the Kyoho period (1716-1764).

``Kingaisha''''
There are the following shrines outside the precincts, and all of them are Shikinai shrines. In "Gogun Shrine Record", the two main shrines and the following four princes are called ``Yutomi Rokusho Shrine''.
* Komori Shrine - Deity enshrined: {{ill|Ō no Yasumaro|be|О-но Ясумара|ca|Ō no Yasumaro|ckb|ئۆ نۆ یاسومارۆ|de|Ō no Yasumaro|eo|O no Jasumaro|es|Ō no Yasumaro|fa|اونو یاسومارو|fr|Ō no Yasumaro|gl|Ō-No-Yasumaro|it|Ō no Yasumaro|ja|太安万侶|ko|오노 야스마로|oc|O no Yasumaro|pl|Ō-no Yasumaro|pt|Ō no Yasumaro|ru|О-но Ясумаро|uk|О но Ясумаро|zh|太安萬侶|qid=Q384705|lt=Taichōshin Yasumanro}}, Shikinai Kosha/Kosha Kamimei Shrine
* Ojijin no Mikoto Shrine - Enshrined deity: Oshijin no Mikoto, Shikinai Small Shrine/Ojijin no Mikoto Shrine (Ronsha)
* Himeji no Mikoto Shrine - Enshrined deity: Himeji no Mikoto, Shikinai small shrine/Himeoji no Mikoto Shrine (Ronsha)
* Yanari Shrine - Enshrined deity: Yanari Shrine, Shikinai Small Shrine/Yanari Shrine

=== Festival ===
The grand festival is held on the third Sunday in April and is called Ohrenzo (the festival is called Renzo in Yamato). In the era when {{ill|Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|Q11511066|qid=Q11511066}} was used, the festival was held around {{ill|Chunfen|Q1339268|qid=Q1339268}}.
